雷.meaning: A sky giant, bored by a week of <part>rain</part>, pulls a square <part>rice field</part> tight like a drum skin and pounds it with both fists. Every boom rattles the farmhouse windows and sends the ducks diving. Below, everyone covers their ears at the <kanji>thunder</kanji>.
雷.on: A <sound>rhi</sound>no in the next field charges at every boom, sure the sky is picking a fight.
雷.kun: Each boom flips a <sound>ca</sound>rp out of the pond onto a <sound>mee</sound>rkat holding a stack of <sound>na</sound>an by the <sound>ree</sound>ds.

載.meaning: A knight on moving day jams his long <part>halberd</part> across the <part>car</part> roof as a rack, then ties on his armour, a harp, a goat and his granny's armchair. The tyres squash flat and the car groans down the lane under its <kanji>load</kanji>.
載.on: At the first bump a jug of <sound>ci</sound>der rolls off the top and soaks the goat.
載.kun: He squeezes in behind the wheel, though there's <sound>no</sound>t much room left for a knight.

述.meaning: A tour guide wheels a potted <part>apple tree</part> up a <part>ramp</part> onto the museum stage, then talks for an hour about every apple on it: its name, its birthday, its favourite song. No fruit goes without a <kanji>mention</kanji>.
述.on: At last a <sound>ju</sound>ry of visitors in the front row stands and drowns him out with a <sound>tsu</sound>nami of clapping.
述.kun: He reads it all from a long scroll tied in a <sound>kno</sound>t, and every apple is on it.

湿.meaning: On a birthday in the jungle, the <part>sun</part> hides behind steam, <part>water drops</part> bead on everything, and the <part>candles</part> on the cake just fizz and refuse to light. The guests' hair goes frizzy and the paper hats droop. Everything is <kanji>damp</kanji>.
湿.on: Grandma throws a bed <sound>shee</sound>t over the cake to keep it dry, and it sticks to the icing.
湿.kun: A soggy <sound>shee</sound>p shakes itself dry all over the <sound>me</sound>lon slices.

倍.meaning: A street speaker hangs her hat on a <part>coat hook</part>, climbs onto her <part>soapbox</part> and shouts, 'Clap for me!' Each clap makes the box grow: two boxes, four, eight, until she's waving above the rooftops. Every cheer makes it <kanji>double</kanji>.
倍.on: To get down, she rides a <sound>bi</sound>ke with two front wheels along the top of the stack.

酷.meaning: A sly chef bakes a candle shaped like a stick of <part>dynamite</part> into his rival's cake, then rushes in to <part>tell</part> the whole room it's about to blow. Guests dive under the tables and leave the cake alone; it was only a candle. What a <kanji>cruel</kanji> joke.
酷.on: Only a <sound>coc</sound>katoo stays at the table and pecks up the whole cake, fuse and all.
酷.kun: The rival's mum stamps her <sound>hee</sound>l and calls a <sound>do</sound>ctor to check her son's nerves.

躍.meaning: At a garden wedding, a shy <part>peacock</part> steps on a sun-baked paving stone, and its scorched <part>foot</part> fires it straight up: tail open, feathers spinning, clean over the cake. The guests clap for the bird's mighty <kanji>leap</kanji>.
躍.on: It lands right on a spiky <sound>yuc</sound>ca and leaps again, even higher.
躍.kun: An <sound>o</sound>tter who is a <sound>do</sound>ctor tapes the foot, and the peacock dances off.

如.meaning: A <part>woman</part> holds up a puppet with a painted <part>mouth</part> and makes it talk in her exact voice. It laughs her laugh and sneezes her sneeze, until the audience can't tell which is which. The puppet is her perfect <kanji>likeness</kanji>.
如.on: A <sound>jo</sound>gger runs past the stage and waves to both of them, just to be safe.
如.kun: The puppet even wears tiny <sound>go</sound>ggles and a <sound>to</sound>p hat, just like hers.

範.meaning: A kid carves a tiny <part>car</part> into the end of a <part>bamboo</part> stick, fits it into a rubber <part>stamp</part> handle and presses it across the kitchen wall in neat rows: car, car, car. Mum comes home to a brand new wallpaper <kanji>pattern</kanji>.
範.on: The kid dipped the stamp in <sound>hon</sound>ey instead of ink, so every little car is sticky.

豊.meaning: A café jukebox is broken in the best way: drop in a coin and it plays its <part>melody</part>, then pours out <part>beans</part>: coffee beans, jelly beans, baked beans, until they flood the floor. Nobody in town goes hungry. The café is <kanji>bountiful</kanji>.
豊.on: Every night the owner sprays the bean flood out the door with a garden <sound>ho</sound>se.
豊.kun: Today a <sound>yu</sound>zu and a warm <sound>ta</sound>co tumble out of the jukebox too.

灰.meaning: A dragon toasts marshmallows on the edge of a <part>cliff</part>, then sneezes into his own <part>fire</part>. Puff: the marshmallows, the sticks and his eyebrows all turn to grey powder that drifts over the edge like snow. Supper is now <kanji>ashes</kanji>.
灰.on: The wind lifts the grey cloud like a <sound>ki</sound>te and carries it out over the sea.
灰.kun: '<sound>Hi</sound>,' says a seagull flying out of the cloud, grey from beak to tail.

鉱.meaning: A mole digging herself a new bedroom hits a streak of <part>gold</part> as <part>wide</part> as a road, studded with glittering rocks of every colour. She labels each lump like a museum: 'Mole's first <kanji>mineral</kanji>.'
鉱.on: She pays for an ice cream <sound>co</sound>ne with one sparkly pebble.
鉱.kun: '<sound>Ah</sound>!' gasps the jeweller, and pays her in <sound>ra</sound>men, <sound>ga</sound>rlic and a <sound>ne</sound>cklace.

滞.meaning: Someone's dressing-gown <part>sash</part> slips down the bath plug and wedges there. The <part>water drops</part> stop going anywhere: the bath sits full for a week, green and still, and a frog moves in. The water begins to <kanji>stagnate</kanji>.
滞.on: Dad tries to hook the sash out with his <sound>tie</sound>, and loses that down the drain too.
滞.kun: The frog puts on a <sound>to</sound>p hat, calls a <sound>do</sound>ctor and orders an ice cream <sound>co</sound>ne.

貯.meaning: A <part>shellfish</part> living under the <part>roof</part> of a bus shelter on a busy <part>street</part> snaps shut on every coin people drop. In ten years its shell is too heavy to open, so it rents a bank vault. Those are serious <kanji>savings</kanji>.
貯.on: It flies to the bank in a rented <sound>cho</sound>pper, clinking all the way.
貯.kun: It pays the pilot with one cold <sound>ta</sound>co from the bus shelter bin.

需.meaning: In a drought, the whole village marches up the hill to an old hermit whose <part>beard</part> is said to summon <part>rain</part> when tugged. They chant, wave signs and refuse to leave until he gives it a pull. Their thirsty crops make it a <kanji>demand</kanji>.
需.on: A <sound>ju</sound>ry of farmers votes that he must tug it twice a week.

壇.meaning: At <part>daybreak</part>, a gardener heaps <part>soil</part> into a tall mound, caps it with a pot <part>lid</part> and fits a motor so the whole thing can <part>revolve</part>. The mayor climbs on and turns slowly as she speaks, facing every corner of the crowd from her new <kanji>podium</kanji>.
壇.on: Her big plan? Turning the old <sound>dun</sound>geon under the town hall into a library.

臭.meaning: A <part>large</part> hockey bag full of old socks is left in a <part>phone booth</part> all summer. Nobody can make a call now: one sniff of the receiver and they stagger back with watering eyes. Even the flies keep away. The booth is <kanji>stinking</kanji>.
臭.on: Inside the bag, one giant <sound>shoe</sound> is the worst of all.
臭.kun: A <sound>coo</sound>k in a <sound>sa</sound>ri holds her nose and sprays the booth with lemon juice.

昔.meaning: Under a museum floor, a cleaner finds a stone <part>pole</part> with <part>two</part> crossbars carved on it, a <part>sun</part> below them and the numeral <part>one</part> scratched at the base: the oldest calendar ever found. Dust puffs out of it like a sigh. It's a note from deep <kanji>antiquity</kanji>.
昔.on: Beside the sun is a scratched <sound>shar</sound>k: there were sharks back then, too.
昔.kun: Below it are carvings of a <sound>moo</sound>se, a <sound>ca</sound>rp and a <sound>shee</sound>p, all long gone from that valley.

狂.meaning: A <part>king</part> swaps his sceptre for a <part>fishhook</part> and starts casting from the palace balcony, hooking hats, pigeons and the chancellor's wig, cackling all the while. The court whispers that he's become a <kanji>lunatic</kanji>.
狂.on: Then he announces the palace is moving to <sound>Kyo</sound>to, dragging out the first part of the name for a full minute.
狂.kun: The palace <sound>coo</sound>k hides in the pantry with her pet <sound>roo</sound>k until it's over.

奪.meaning: A <part>bird rider</part> swoops over the golf course and snatches a player's <part>golf club</part> in mid-swing, flapping off with it while the ball dribbles into the pond. The golfer shakes his fist at the sky. What a way to <kanji>rob</kanji> a man.
奪.on: A <sound>du</sound>ck in the pond gets bonked by the ball and quacks up a <sound>tsu</sound>nami of splashes.
奪.kun: The bird circles back and steals his <sound>u</sound>don lunch too. '<sound>Bah</sound>!' groans the golfer.

履.meaning: A one-man band plants his <part>flag</part> in the square and promises to <part>restore</part> any broken toy while juggling it. Teddies get stitched in mid-air, and a train gets its wheel back on the third throw. Every night he loves to <kanji>perform</kanji>.
履.on: His best trick is juggling three chunks of coral from a <sound>ree</sound>f without dropping one.
履.kun: For his encore he puts on shoes shaped like a <sound>ha</sound>rp and dances a jig in them.

募.meaning: A circus strongwoman flexes one <part>muscle</part> on the beach at <part>sunset</part>, and its shadow stretches across every sunbather. Amazed, they sign up for her troupe on the spot. That's how she likes to <kanji>recruit</kanji>.
募.on: Her first recruit balances a <sound>bo</sound>nsai on his nose all the way to the tent.
募.kun: Another joins by surfing in on a <sound>tsu</sound>nami, which is <sound>no</sound>t easy to do.

章.meaning: The scout leader sets the camp <part>chime</part> to ring absurdly <part>early</part>, at three in the morning. The one kid who is already up, dressed and toasting crumpets wins a shiny new sew-on <kanji>badge</kanji>.
章.on: She shows it off at the campfire <sound>show</sound> that night, and everyone claps.

恥.meaning: A knight admits in front of the whole court that he's scared of moths. His <part>heart</part> sinks into his boots and each <part>ear</part> glows so red it lights the hall like a lamp. He wishes the floor would swallow him: pure <kanji>shame</kanji>.
恥.on: Even his pet <sound>chee</sound>tah hides its face behind its tail.
恥.kun: Just then a moth flutters out of his helmet. '<sound>Ha</sound>!' snorts the queen.

肝.meaning: A goose who ate a whole wheel of rich cheese lies groaning under the <part>moon</part>. Her friends drape her over a <part>drying rack</part> to recover, like a damp towel. 'Poor thing,' says the doctor duck. 'It's her <kanji>liver</kanji>.'
肝.on: Her friends tuck a pink <sound>car</sound>nation into the rack to cheer her up.
肝.kun: Then they feed her one <sound>ki</sound>wi and wipe her beak with a <sound>mo</sound>p.

姿.meaning: Behind the sheet at a shadow show, a <part>woman</part> strikes a pose, then the <part>next</part>: a teapot, a swan, a rocket. The children shout out each shape her outline makes. You never see her face, only her <kanji>figure</kanji>.
姿.on: For the last pose she holds up a knight's <sound>shie</sound>ld and the kids cheer.
姿.kun: At the break she hands out <sound>su</sound>shi, <sound>ga</sound>rlic bread and <sound>ta</sound>cos.

兆.meaning: On a frozen lake, a skating heron's <part>legs</part> wobble as the <part>ice</part> beneath it cracks into the exact shape of a lightning bolt. The village elders gasp and cancel the winter fair. A crack like that is a <kanji>portent</kanji>.
兆.on: Next day the mayor wears a lucky <sound>cho</sound>ker of ice cubes to keep bad luck away.
兆.kun: The elders sell lucky <sound>ki</sound>wis at a ba<sound>za</sound>ar to ward off whatever is coming.

焦.meaning: A <part>sparrow</part> judging a barbecue contest hops right over the <part>hot coals</part> to sniff each sausage, until its tail feathers start to smoke. It flutters off unhurt, but the sausages nobody flipped turn black. They <kanji>char</kanji>.
焦.on: The crowd thinks it was all part of the <sound>show</sound> and claps.
焦.kun: A <sound>ko</sound>ala judge eats the burnt ones anyway and gives them full marks.

響.meaning: A homesick sailor taps a tiny <part>chime</part> on a ship far out at sea, and three days later the ding bounces off the hills of his <part>home town</part>. His mum answers by banging a pan. Whatever you ring comes back as an <kanji>echo</kanji>.
響.on: His sister calls back from a trip to <sound>Kyo</sound>to, shouting its name so the first part rolls on and on.
響.kun: The ding shakes a <sound>hee</sound>l off a boot and a <sound>bee</sound>tle off a leaf.

粗.meaning: A cheap hotel stuffs its pillows with uncooked <part>rice</part> and stacks them in a wobbly tower, one on another, under a sign: 'And <part>moreover</part>, one more!' Guests wake with dented, scratched cheeks. The bedding is awfully <kanji>coarse</kanji>.
粗.on: Most guests give up and sleep on the lobby <sound>so</sound>fa instead.
粗.kun: '<sound>Ah</sound>,' sighs one guest, 'next time stuff them with soft <sound>ra</sound>men.'
